cards.stem: What condition lets an aircraft keep steady airspeed in level flight under the first law?
cards.quote: Since there is no net external force on the aircraft, the aircraft maintains a constant airspeed as described by Newton’s First Law of Motion.
cards.hint: Consider when forces balance to zero

cards.stem: Which force equality is required for steady level cruise at constant speed?
options: lift is equal to the weight
drag is equal to the lift
weight is equal to the thrust
cards.quote: an airplane can maintain a constant speed and level flight, in which the lift is equal to the weight, and the thrust is equal to the drag.
cards.hint: Level flight pairs vertical forces together

cards.stem: When does ground speed stay steady during cruise?
cards.quote: The ground speed remains constant as long as the wind speed is constant.
cards.hint: Ground speed depends on air motion relative to surface

cards.stem: What determines the greatest distance an aircraft can fly before refueling?
options: ground speed times the maximum time
ground speed divided by time aloft
cards.quote: The maximum distance that the aircraft can fly is then equal to the ground speed times the maximum time (tmax).
cards.hint: Maximum distance uses longest time aloft
